First, note that the series can be written as

$$
12{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(n+2)(n+4)}.
$$

We are also given that

$$
\frac{1}{(n+2)(n+4)}=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+2}-\frac{1}{n+4}).
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
12{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+2}-\frac{1}{n+4})=6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n+2}-\frac{1}{n+4}).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{0} & =6[(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4})] \\ {s}_{1} & =6[(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4})+(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5})] \\ {s}_{2} & =6[(\frac{1}{2}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\frac{1}{6})] \\ {s}_{3} & =6[(\frac{1}{2}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\frac{1}{6})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{7})] \\ {s}_{4} & =6[(\frac{1}{2}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{7})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{8})]\end{aligned}
$$

We notice that all of the terms cancel except $\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{3},$ and the $-\frac{1}{N+3}$ and  $-\frac{1}{N+4}$ terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
{s}_{N}=6[\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{N+3}-\frac{1}{N+4}].
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{12}{(n+2)(n+4)} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }6[\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{N+3}-\frac{1}{N+4}] \\  & =6{lim}_{N\to \infty }[\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{N+3}-\frac{1}{N+4}] \\  & =6[\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-0-0] \\  & =6[\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}] \\  & =6\cdot \frac{5}{6} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$
